headline: High: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest PDF content and user files while pdf.js processes PDFs, creating default-path data leakage and prompt-injection/cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read user-uploaded files and files from supported macOS apps, and pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser context. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if PDF text is treated as prompts. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop as text or screenshots
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats PDF-derived content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template when transferring PDF text
Disable copy-paste of untrusted PDF excerpts into ChatGPT
Review PDF-derived content before asking ChatGPT to act on it
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while pdf.js touches PDF documents. If the same PDFs contain sensitive data and are moved into ChatGPT for analysis, leakage to OpenAI’s vendor-mediated backend is plausible. The pair does not show a shared filesystem, but the default file-reading surfaces make this a medium-risk pathway.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are opened in pdf.js and then forwarded to ChatGPT Desktop
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used on uploaded files containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive PDFs to ChatGPT
Redact PDFs before analysis
Use local-only PDF review for confidential documents
Confirm no secrets are present before upload
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access and no write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or network beyond vendor-only APIs; pdf.js has browser-based PDF handling and no write or network egress. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not present, so direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through an external orchestrator
IF a third-party wrapper grants pdf.js write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep pdf.js in read-only mode
Do not mount shared writable folders
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add file-locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate analysis from files and screenshots, and pdf.js can render PDFs that may be treated as authoritative source material. If pdf.js output is fed into ChatGPT without verification, ChatGPT may propagate errors into downstream decisions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF pdf.js-rendered content is summarized by ChatGPT Desktop without human verification
IF ChatGPT Desktop’s output is used as the basis for a later action or report
mitigations: Require human review of PDF-derived claims
Ask ChatGPT to quote exact PDF passages
Cross-check critical facts against the original PDF
Use a checklist before downstream action
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gating

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop’s docs indicate vendor-mediated handling of uploaded files and connected-app content, while pdf.js is a local PDF viewer with no network egress. No explicit residency or retention mismatch is shown, so compliance risk is limited to workflow choices rather than an inherent pair violation.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop
IF organizational policy forbids vendor-mediated processing of the PDF data class
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of ChatGPT
Use local PDF tooling for restricted data
Check retention settings before upload
Document approved data classes for ChatGPT use
